Frontend Playwright: 28/30 checks pass — page loads at /qc-tests, all 5 filter/table testids present (qc-download-excel-btn, qc-search-input, qc-sample-type-filter, qc-result-filter, qc-tests-table), APR-003 search shows exactly 6 rows with individual testids qc-row-{20L,600S}-APR-003-{1,2,3}, no qc-retest-* buttons (all trials already passed), qc-delete-20L-APR-003-3 exists but qc-delete-...1 does NOT (attempt 1 undeletable), Production filter shows 36 rows, edit dialog opens, result select disabled for Production sample with all 5 qc-edit-* testids visible, saving reviewed_date<testing_date surfaces sonner toast 'Reviewed Date must be on or after the Testing Date' from a 400 backend response, /water-intelligence loads for admin without redirect and renders Pending/Approved/Published/Rejected/All tabs with the Water Intelligence sidebar link highlighted (visual confirmation via screenshot). critical_code_review_comments: qc_tests.py _sync() uses len(have)==0 to decide first-seed 94/6 split. If ALL seeded qc_tests are ever manually deleted from mongo but production_batches remain, a subsequent GET would re-run the trial-heavy first-seed logic on the entire batch set (unexpectedly recreating trial attempts). Consider tracking a persistent 'first_seed_done' flag on tenant settings.

PUT /qc-tests/{id} when converting trial→production silently forces attempt=1 without renumbering, which could create a duplicate attempt if the batch already has an attempt-1 record from the previous trial history. Guarded partially by 'batch_attempts>1' check (blocks conversion when >1 attempts exist), but still worth an explicit unique(batch_id, attempt) index in mongo.

Frontend latestAttempt map is computed from the currently-FILTERED rows, so when result=reject filter is active the retest button may appear on a row that isn't actually the true latest attempt in the DB. Backend guards this correctly (add_retest fetches all attempts and checks latest.test_result), but the UI can be misleading. Consider computing latestAttempt server-side or fetching per-batch attempts.
Excel export re-runs _sync() on every download call — for tenants with 2000+ batches this is a wasteful DB scan on a click-through endpoint. Sync-on-list is enough; export can skip.
